chunks: From him, from Ḥusayn ibn Hāshim, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the one bereft of his family and wealth is the one who neglects the ʿaṣr salat (prayer).” I said: “What is the bereft one?” He said: “He will have no family and no wealth in Paradise.” I said: “What is neglecting it?” He said: “He leaves it until the sun turns yellow and sets.”

key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, where the deprived person will have no family or wealth
key_terms.الْمَوْتُورَ: the one who is deprived and left bereft
key_terms.تَصْفَرَّ: to become yellow, referring to the sun near sunset
key_terms.تَضْيِيعُهَا: neglecting it by wasting or missing its proper time
key_terms.تَغِيبَ: to set, meaning the disappearance of the sun

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about delaying or neglecting the ʿaṣr salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith warns severely against neglecting the ʿaṣr salat (prayer), describing such a person as truly bereft. It explains that wasting this salat (prayer) means delaying it until the sun yellows and disappears, and it links such neglect to deprivation in Paradise.
